text:
Nina: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: capacity & regions. Two asks: can leadership confirm ETA for APAC prewarm lanes and what's the customer-visible fallback if procurement slips?

Rahul: APAC prewarm lanes are targeted for late Q2 pending rack delivery and regional validation. If procurement slips we'll rely on a three-tier fallback: (1) short-term prefix cache + quantized variants, (2) burst buckets (reserved capacity) remapped, (3) cross-region failover to nearest healthy zone.

Omar: Important for CS: which customers are in burst buckets vs prewarm-eligible? We need a list to update status pages.

Sofie: There's a new console widget under infra->regions->capacity-map that shows prewarm eligiblity and burst allocations. I'll export CSV and share with CS by EOD.

Nina: Can someone post a blurb PMs can use to explain user impact?

Rahul: Copy for PMs: "If APAC prewarm isn't available, interactive p95/p99 may increase 100-350ms while autoscaler ramps. For sustained high load, requests will hit burst buckets or be routed to nearby regions which may add network latency. We prioritize customer SLAs and reserved capacity where applicable."

Omar: Ops note: fallback playbook abbreviated below, full runbook in Confluence.
```
# abbreviated fallback
on procurement.delay:
  enable_quantized_routing()
  set_batch_size(target=small)
  remap_reserved_buckets()
  notify #infra #support
```

CapacityBot: Playbook page created: https://confluence.redwood/infra/capacity-fallbacks :white_check_mark:

Nina: Great, thanks. Action items: Sofie to send CSV to CS, Rahul to add APAC prewarm status to roadmap doc, Omar to flag high-risk customers for mitigation. I'll follow up after we have the CSV. :thumbsup:
